outcome: success of trial of labor after cesarean section (TOLAC), categorized as vaginal delivery or cesarean delivery
cohort: Women with antepartum fetal death diagnosed at or beyond 34 weeks gestation and with one previous low transverse cesarean section, attempting a trial of labor.
finding: A nomogram developed using non-linear classifiers and maternal predelivery features (BMI, Bishop score, duration of augmentation, estimated fetal weight, interval from previous LTCS, admission to active labor interval, vaginal delivery after LTCS, gestational age) was able to predict the outcome of TOLAC (vaginal vs. cesarean delivery) in women with intra-uterine fetal death at or beyond 34 weeks gestation with high accuracy (0.88).
mod_finding: The study developed a predictive nomogram to determine the probability of successful vaginal birth versus cesarean delivery among women with antepartum fetal death undergoing TOLAC.
